about.title: Alameda Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A faulty product doesn't announce itself. It might be a space heater bought for a drafty rental off Central Avenue, a child's car seat, a pressure cooker, or a set of brakes on a car that travels Lincoln Avenue or Buena Vista Avenue. When something you trusted fails and hurts you, the question in Alameda is rarely who was careless. Under California's strict liability rules, you generally do not have to prove the manufacturer was negligent. You need to show the product had a defect in its design, its manufacturing, or its warnings, and that the defect caused your injury. Responsibility can also reach beyond the company whose name is on the box: distributors and the retailer that sold it, whether a Park Street shop or an online seller, may share liability. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects injured Alameda County residents with an independent product liability attorney who handles cases on contingency. Step one: keep the product exactly as it is.

whyChoose.title: Why Alameda Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict liability changes the burden
items.desc: In most California product cases you show the defect and the harm it caused, not a careless act. An attorney familiar with that standard can frame your Alameda claim accordingly from the start.

items.title: Every link in the chain matters
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the local or online retailer that sold the item may all be answerable. Your matched attorney can sort out who belongs in the claim.

items.title: Evidence-first guidance, no fee up front
items.desc: The product itself is usually the single most important piece of evidence, and we stress preserving it before anything else. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there is no fee unless you recover.

items.question: I bought the item at a shop on Park Street. Is the store responsible, or only the manufacturer?
items.answer: Both can be. California's strict liability doctrine reaches manufacturers, distributors, and retailers, so the Alameda store that sold the product may be part of the claim even though it did not make the item. Which parties are ultimately pursued depends on the facts, and that is something your matched attorney will evaluate.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company knew the product was unsafe?
items.answer: Generally, no. Under strict liability you typically need to establish that the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that the defect caused your injury. Whether the maker acted carelessly is usually not the central question, though an attorney can advise how your specific situation fits.

items.question: My car crash in Alameda may have involved a defective part. Is that a product case or an auto case?
items.answer: It can be both. Alameda recorded 129 injury collisions in 2025, and when a component such as an airbag, tire, or brake system fails, a product liability claim may sit alongside a standard auto claim. Keep the vehicle and the suspect part unaltered if you can, and let an attorney assess the overlap before any repairs or salvage.
